guards.what: N1: `creature == base.Owner.Creature` (SparklingRouge.cs:31) vs the sim's `on_block_cleared` firing for enemies too
guards.rationale: Re-read after G1's closure: `sparkling_rouge.py` has no explicit `target is self.player` guard of its own, unlike its two hook-siblings (`captains_wheel.py`, `horn_cleat.py`), which is worth flagging rather than silently correct -- `combat.py`'s enemy arm (`combat.py:544-553`) also calls `on_block_cleared(enemy)`, so an unguarded listener here WOULD fire for enemy clears too. Checked the method signature: `sparkling_rouge.py:19` is `def on_block_cleared(self, player: PlayerCombatState) -> None`, i.e. it is dispatched only through the PLAYER'S OWN `start_turn` call site (`player.py:223`), not through the shared multi-target hook the two siblings' explicit checks guard against -- so the omission is safe by construction, not by a missing guard, and no enemy-side call ever reaches this method. C#'s `creature == base.Owner.Creature` check on the shared hook is structurally satisfied the same way the siblings assert it explicitly.

Both sides now read the turn number at the SAME point in the turn (G1's slot fix), so there is no longer even a same-turn-different-position question to check -- `self.turn` at `on_block_cleared` is the value `CombatManager.cs:500-507`'s loop sees too. EXECUTED (round 11 probe, sparkling-rouge-slot): triggers on turn 3 and only turn 3.

guards.what: N3: PowerVar<StrengthPower>(1m) and PowerVar<DexterityPower>(1m) read as BaseValue (SparklingRouge.cs:17-21, 34-35), the ORDER of the two applications, and the applier
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in SparklingRouge.cs, so both BaseValues are the pinned non-ascension 1 and sparkling_rouge.py:23-24's literal 1s are correct. Order matches too (Strength then Dexterity), which is checked deliberately because relic/ruined_helmet doubles the FIRST Strength gain of a combat and a swapped order would not change that here (Dexterity is not Strength). C# passes applier = Owner.Creature on both calls (SparklingRouge.cs:34-35) and so does the port (`applier=player`), which matters for relic/unsettling_lamp: its doubling needs `applier is self.player and target is not self.player` (unsettling_lamp.py:47) and the target here IS the player, so neither side doubles.
